themes_detail.label: Dead Animals & Animal Abuse Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Central Harlem is experiencing a dramatic spike in animal-related complaints this week and last week: 3 dead animal reports last week (700% above the 0.4-complaint weekly average) and 9 animal abuse reports 2 weeks ago (213% above the 2.9-complaint average), suggesting a potential public health or animal welfare emergency requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: Dead animal complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Animal abuse complaints: 9 two weeks ago vs. 2.9 weekly average (213% spike, z-score 6.61)
Unsanitary animal private property complaints: 4 last week vs. 1.5 weekly average (167% spike, z-score 3.54)
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD Animal Cruelty Investigators and local animal rescue organizations about the spike; map complaint locations to identify hotspots
Investigate whether recent weather, food waste management failures, or a specific incident (e.g., animal hoarding, sanctuary closure) triggered the surge

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Over the past week, illegal tree damage complaints jumped to 4 reports, a 357% increase above the 0.9-complaint weekly baseline (z-score 4.0), indicating possible construction activity, unpermitted landscape work, or organized tree removal that warrants enforcement attention.
evidence: Illegal tree damage: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (357% spike, z-score 4.0)
Context: 490 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (416 alterations) suggest ongoing construction activity that may correlate with tree damage
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 4 tree damage complaints with active DOB permits and ULURP applications (254 West 124th Street, One45 for Harlem) to identify which projects are causing damage
Interview NYC Parks Department about enforcement actions; determine if illegal tree removal is tied to development or contractor negligence

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Spike
themes_detail.summary: Central Harlem recorded 4 food poisoning complaints 2 weeks ago, a 220% increase above the 1.2-complaint weekly average (z-score 3.32), suggesting a possible foodborne illness outbreak or restaurant health code violations that public health authorities should investigate.
evidence: Food poisoning complaints: 4 two weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (220% spike, z-score 3.32)
No corroborating Reddit discussion or recent news coverage, suggesting story may be under-reported
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to identify which restaurants or food vendors were cited; determine if complaints cluster around specific establishments or cuisines
Interview affected residents about symptoms and onset timeline to assess whether this represents a genuine outbreak or isolated incidents

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal & Waste Management Failure
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints reached 9 reports 2 weeks ago, a 188% spike above the 3.1-complaint average (z-score 3.82), pointing to a potential neighborhood-wide waste collection breakdown or illegal dumping problem that intersects with the 700% surge in dead animal complaints.
evidence: Residential disposal complaints: 9 two weeks ago vs. 3.1 weekly average (188% spike, z-score 3.82)
Convergence signal: disposal spike + dead animal spike + unsanitary condition complaints (1,222 in 90 days) suggest systemic waste management failure
Long-standing CB budget request for DEP capital improvements suggests infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Investigate whether Sanitation Department service cuts or route changes affected Central Harlem; compare collection schedules and complaint locations
Report on whether waste mismanagement is creating conditions that attract rodents and other animals, connecting the disposal and dead animal spikes

themes_detail.label: Water System Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints spiked to 22 reports 3 weeks ago, a 171% increase above the 8.1-complaint average (z-score 3.6), coinciding with the 3,362 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days, suggesting potential widespread plumbing or municipal water delivery failures affecting residents.
evidence: Water system complaints: 22 three weeks ago vs. 8.1 weekly average (171% spike, z-score 3.6)
Heat/hot water complaints dominate 90-day dataset at 3,362 (highest complaint category), with plumbing complaints at 763
Long-standing CB budget request for DEP capital budget improvements indicates chronic infrastructure underinvestment
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to identify main breaks, pressure issues, or service disruptions in Central Harlem during the spike period
Interview residents about simultaneous loss of hot water and water pressure; investigate whether outages correlate with specific buildings or blocks
